features: WHAT JUNE DRAGGED ALONG WITH IT — The F24 module shipped in beta.38 and the printable form in beta.39. Before going further we took the Italian Revenue Agency's own texts and checked them against the code, rule by rule, demanding for every claim the exact line that implements it. Almost everything held; one thing did not, and it concerned the deadlines — the part that carries penalties.
NO DATABASE CHANGES: no migrations, no data rewritten.

Fixed — A WITHHOLDING PAID BETWEEN 1 AND 15 JUNE DRAGGED ALL THOSE FROM JANUARY TO MAY WITH IT, ALL THE WAY TO 16 DECEMBER. 16 June is a statutory deadline: it closes whatever was withheld up to May, even if the total stayed below € 500. The software closed the group only if the NEXT withholding fell AFTER 16 June — and one dated 10 June falls before. The result: € 200 withheld in March was scheduled for 16 December instead of 16 June, six months late. The defect was invisible when looking at a single deadline: it took two payments, one earlier and one in the first half of June.

SINCE WHEN, AND HOW TO CHECK: the defect has existed since the module shipped, in beta.38. Draft payment slips are rebuilt from scratch by pressing «Aggiorna scadenze» in the schedule and come out correct from this release, so there is nothing to repair by hand. Anyone who has already recorded a payment following a December date that contained withholdings made before June has paid late and should know it: the payment slip page lists the payments it is covering, with their dates.

Under the hood: the fix does not add a special case for June, it changes the question. It used to ask «does the next withholding fall after the deadline?», it now asks «does the next withholding belong to the same window?» — which is what the rule actually says, and holds for any window without listing them. The same defect on the December window had already been fixed during beta.38, when a test surfaced it: back then the case was fixed, and the twin June window stayed broken for a whole cycle. That is why this time the fix lives in the general rule. Five new tests: the 10 June case, the exact 16 June boundary, and three counter-checks verifying that two withholdings in the same window still stay in a single slip.
